As an adult, it never really went away, though I learned to hide it some. Now, at 78, I’m restless all the time—can’t sit through a sermon or even a meal without getting up, pacing, needing to do *something*. I feel like I’m driven, like a motor’s running inside me. I’ll start cleaning, then remember something else, start that, and nothing gets finished. I lose track of what I’m doing halfway through. My daughter says I interrupt her mid-sentence, jump into her stories, and I know it frustrates her, but I just can’t hold it in.  

Recently, I’ve felt more on edge, more talkative than usual, like my thoughts are racing. My son mentioned I seemed “high,” but this hyperactivity? It’s been with me since I was a child, long before any of these mood spells. This isn’t new—it’s always been there, steady, like a background hum. The mood stuff comes and goes, but the restlessness, the needing to move, the interrupting—it’s always there.
D003-D008_h023.options:
A. Bipolar I Disorder
    B. Delusional Disorder
    C. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    D. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Predominantly Hyperactive/Impulsive Presentation)

D003-D008_h024.question:
I’ve always felt like I never quite fit in, even as a kid. Teachers used to say I was “wired” — I couldn’t stay in my seat during class, and I was always blurting out answers or jumping into other kids’ games. Looking back, I realize that never really went away. Now, at 39, I don’t run around the office, but inside, I feel this constant restlessness, like I’m being pushed forward by some engine I can’t turn off. I’m always pacing during phone calls, tapping, fidgeting — my coworkers joke I’m never still.  

I know I interrupt people. I don’t mean to, but my mind races, and I’ll jump into conversations before someone finishes. It’s caused problems — with customers, ex-co-workers, even my ex-wife. Staying focused is another struggle. Deals fall through because I lose track of details, and I can’t organize my schedule to save my life. It’s been like this since I was a kid — definitely before I was 12.  

Now and then, I do get these bursts where I feel super confident, talk fast, need less sleep — almost like a manic high. But even when those pass, the restlessness, the impulsivity, the constant motion? That’s always there.
D003-D008_h024.options:
A. Bipolar I Disorder
    B. Delusional Disorder
    C. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    D. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Predominantly Hyperactive/Impulsive Presentation)

D003-D008_h025.question:
I’ve always been this way—even as a kid, my teachers said I couldn’t sit still, always tapping, fidgeting, or getting up during class. Now at 53, I don’t run around, but I still feel restless inside, like I can’t turn my body off. My studio is chaotic—half-finished jewelry pieces everywhere—because I start projects but lose focus fast. I want to finish them, but I get distracted easily, and organizing my workflow feels impossible.  

At meetings or even social gatherings, I catch myself blurting out thoughts before people finish talking. I don’t mean to interrupt, but the words just come out. I’ll stand up mid-conversation, walk over to my bench, start adjusting a design—my body won’t stay still.  

About two years ago, I had a period where I felt unusually high—racing thoughts, barely sleeping, spending money on materials I didn’t need. But even before that, and now that it’s passed, the restlessness and impulsivity never went away. That’s what makes me think it’s not just the mood episode—it’s been with me my whole life, steady, like a motor always running.
D003-D008_h025.options:
A. Bipolar I Disorder
    B. Delusional Disorder
    C. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    D. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Predominantly Hyperactive/Impulsive Presentation)
